title: Graduate old Alpha metrics to Beta
body:
### What would you like to be added?

Before introduction of Beta metric stability, we had many important metrics that were stuck in Alpha state.

Would like to propose a list of metric candidates that should be reviewed for graduation to Beta.

We would still review each metric individually for any antipattern, but fact they are in use for so long should be good enough reason for graduation. 

Graduation criteria are at https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/9de615daee15bdee370a825dc0ef150eac189700/contributors/devel/sig-instrumentation/metric-instrumentation.md#graduating-to-beta

Subtasks:
* https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/136304
* https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/136305
* https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/136306
* https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/136307
* https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/136308
* https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/136310
* https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/136311
* https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/136312
* https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/136313

### Why is this needed?

Those metrics have been already present in K8s for long time and are at use by GKE. 

While we won't necessarily want to graduate them GA, marking them as Beta would indicate their importance and allow community to pay more attention to them over other Alpha metrics.

/cc @richabanker @dgrisonnet

title: Service Controller Does Not Reconcile When LoadBalancer Status is Cleared
body:
### What happened?

The cloud-provider service controller doesn't trigger reconciliation when a LoadBalancer Service's status is cleared by external controllers like GitOps tools. This happens when the Service spec includes [INLINE_CODE] and the GitOps tool updates the Service, clearing the status field. Even though the cloud load balancer continues to function normally, the Service shows a pending status indefinitely because the controller only detects changes to the Service spec, not the status.

### What did you expect to happen?

When a LoadBalancer Service's status is cleared during a resource update, the service controller should detect this change and reconcile by querying the cloud provider to restore the correct LoadBalancer ingress information.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Create a LoadBalancer Service with [INLINE_CODE] specified in the spec:

2. Verify the Service has [INLINE_CODE] populated with the LB IP
3. Apply the same Service YAML using a GitOps tool or kubectl, which clears the status field
4. Observe the Service status remains empty/pending even though the cloud load balancer exists and functions correctly

### Anything else we need to know?

The [INLINE_CODE] function in [INLINE_CODE] (lines 557-616) only checks [INLINE_CODE] fields like ports, annotations, and IPs. It doesn't check if [INLINE_CODE] has been cleared.

similar_issues.text: Don't blindly trust cached state of load balancer resources in service controller. multiple users have been bit by some variant of the following problem : they delete a resource from their cloud provider that was created as part of a service's external load balancer. if they deleted it accidentally, they wonder why their load balancer stopped working. if they deleted it intentionally, they wonder why it comes back after an indeterminate amount of time ( typically on the order of days or weeks ). this is caused by us caching the last observed state of the cloud provider resources in the service controller ( with no ttl ) rather than rechecking it periodically, such that it only gets rechecked when the controller manager process is restarted. this confusion isn't worth saving a few cloud api calls, particularly given that most clusters don't expose all that many external services. we might want to include this as a bug fix in 1. 3, but it's not absolutely critical. happy to hear your thoughts on that. @ bprashanth @ thockin @ alex - mohr

CloudProvider reconciler/controller for required dependencies. a number of resources in kubernetes need to be synced with the cloud provider - - disks, vms, load balancers. see e. g. https : / / github. com / googlecloudplatform / kubernetes / issues / 5180 options are : - each xcontroller has a big switch statement and calls out to the appropriate provider when a matching resource needs create / delete / update. for nodes ( vms ), loadbalancers, firewalls, etc. - there's a cloudprovidergcecontroller that's responsible for observing current state of project and updating it to match desired. individual within - cluster controllers only concern themselves with intra - cluster changes.

Warn when missing cloud-provider on kube controller. this commit warns the user / gives better information that when using - - cloud - provider = " " on kube - controller, that services such as loadbalancer will not work. however, despite the error, kube - controller will still run as normal. fixes https : / / github. com / kubernetes / kubernetes / issues / 12716 fixes https : / / github. com / kubernetes / kubernetes / issues / 11172 fixes https : / / github. com / kubernetes / kubernetes / issues / 27085

Handle deleting external load balancers across kube-controller-manager restarts. right now, the service controller has no sense of responsibility for the load balancer resources that exist in a cloud user's project. it only deletes things that it knows it owns, meaning that if it gets restarted while deleting a load balancer, it won't finish deleting the load balancer when it restarts ( or if it's simply not running when a load balancer gets deleted, it won't even start deleting the load balancer ). this should reduce resource leaks, especially in any e2e tests that involve restarting ( including upgrading ) the master. cross - referencing various leak - related issues : # 13515, # 14597, # 15083, # 15084 @ davidopp @ quinton - hoole

title: Define the Gang satisfaction policy for Workload.Spec[i].PodGroup
body:
The current Gang satisfaction policy of the Workload API is relatively simple. At present, Gang member Pods can only get binding opportunities when len(waitingAndAssigned) >= minCount. The code is as follows:

[CODE_BLOCK]

The problem is that the Pod controller does not always want to follow this strategy, but may instead want to follow the following strategy.
1. Some workloads may only want to follow the gang scheduling policy at the initial scheduling stage. Once the workload meets the gang quorum and enters the running state, availability of the workload takes priority over everything else. For example, for a workload with 10 member pods, if two of the member pods are being recreated due to node failures or other reasons, even if the cluster has only one available node, we still want one of the member pods to be scheduled as soon as possible instead of waiting for the quorum to be satisfied. We refer to this strategy as [INLINE_CODE].
2. In another scenario, when a Workload behaves abnormally for some reason, the Pod controller may want to rebuild all Pods while the Workload itself remains. Since the member Pods cannot be rebuilt all at once, during this time, we want the rebuilt Pods to stay in a Waiting state. We refer to this strategy as [INLINE_CODE]. I have seen that WAS envisions using the Workload as a kind of Reservation to pre-allocate resources, rather than being bound to actual Pods. To some extent, this strategy is also beneficial for scenarios where we only want to retain the resources reserved by the Workload, but want to replace all the runtime Pods.

Therefore, this issue aims to define three satisfaction strategies for Gang: [INLINE_CODE], [INLINE_CODE], and the current default [INLINE_CODE]. Looking forward to comments.

similar_issues.text: Schedule a group of pods all at once (aka coscheduling, sometimes known as gang scheduling). like many other schedulers, k8s scheduler is a sequential scheduler handles pods one by one. this makes the architecture and algorithm simpler, but in some cases a sequential scheduler could make worse decisions than a scheduler which takes a group of pods into account, the sequential scheduler is like a “ greedy algorithm ” framework for pods placement. i would like to suggest adding “ group scheduling ” support for the scheduler, and an ” all - or - nothing ” result is reasonable i think. please share your thoughts. thanks! @ davidopp

Prevent evicted pods from being scheduled back onto the same node. add something like [ inline _ code ] to [ inline _ code ] semantics is : if the pod is managed by a replication controller, scheduler will try to put the replacement pod on a node different from the one where the pod you are deleting was previously running. ( if the pod is not managed by a replication controller, then the option has no effect. ) proposed implementation is - add [ inline _ code ] field to [ inline _ code ] - before deleting the pod, api server ( registry, i think ) adds an annotation to the pod ( maybe key [ inline _ code ] and no value ) - modify the controllers so that when they see this annotation added to a pod, they cache the name of the pod p and the name of the node n it is running on ; when they see the deletion and go to create the replacement pod for p, they add a softnodeaffinity for " node name is not n " ( i just realized this feature is dependent on implementation of # 18261 since we can't express this today, and also dependent on exposing node name as a node label which is part of # 9044 ) this should work even if the controller fails between the update and the deletion, but not if the controller fails between the deletion and creating the replacement pod. this should be ok as the feature is " best effort " ( we intentionally use softnodeaffinity instead of hardnodeaffinity ). this is a pre - requisite for rescheduler, so it can create a hole for a pending pod to schedule into, without having the pod that was previously in that hole schedule back into the space first. however there are other uses, for example a human operator might want to move a pod off a node for some reason ( maybe it is receiving or producing interference from / to another pod on that node ). this was originally discussed in this comment https : / / github. com / kubernetes / kubernetes / issues / 12140 # issuecomment - 156282772 cc / @ mikedanese @ lavalamp @ bgrant0607 @ mml assigned to @ haiyangding who said he would implement it ( but note that it is dependent on implementation of # 18261, as well as exposing node name as a node label ).

Add PodSpec.NodeFailurePolicy = {Reschedule, Delete, Ignore}. a start to updating podspec to include nodefailurepolicy, which describes what the user would like the system to do when the pod is unable to run on its bound node, such as when that node is marked as failed or removed from the cluster. nodefailurepolicy may be reschedule, delete, or ignore, with a default policy of reschedule. default behavior will change such that pods reschedule in the presence of node failures by restarting on working nodes instead of being deleted. and if users do not want the default behavior, they're able to opt for deletion - - or completely disable those automatics by setting the policy to ignore and using some other mechanism to react. this pr is only a sketch of the api and discusses the rationale and proposed plan. after general consensus on the overall structure, i'll implement it. plan : update the rest of pkg / api to support this field, add inter - version conversion logic, update the existing pod eviction code in cloudprovider / controller / nodecontroller. go to reschedule or delete based on policy, add tests, and update docs to reflect new usage. i realize we've discussed similar topics before ( most recently # 5353, but also # 5334, # 5335, and # 260 ) with alternate approaches based on philosophical perspectives as to what pods should be, but on further reflection, i think we can do better by our users by meeting them where they are and being pragmatic about allowing pods to survive failures by rescheduling onto other nodes. in particular, pod lifetime becomes bound to cluster lifetime rather than the lifetime of a given node. that change furthers our goal of helping users to think about pods and containers rather than specific nodes. consider two specific use cases : ( 1 ) moving from node to cluster and ( 2 ) resizing a cluster. ( 1 ) if someone is using kubelet ( or docker or monit or supervisord ) on a particular node to keep its containers running, when they transition to kubernetes, they receive a container cluster equivalent and their created pods benefit from the new environment. ( 2 ) with our current behavior, on static clusters composed of robust vms, pods run for a long time. but if the cluster is resized

Fix the "first pod problem" for inter-controller/service pod affinity like we did for same-controller/service pod affinity. in the pod affinity design we identified a problem ( let's call it the " first pod problem " ) where the way you express the rule " run all the pods from service s in the same zone " is to say " each pod from service s should only run in a zone that is already running a pod from service s " ; this works once there is one pod from s running, but the first pod from s will block forever if the rule is taken literally, so nothing will ever schedule. so we have a workaround where we identify this scenario explicitly, and allow the first pod to schedule anywhere. it occurred to me that we have a similar problem if people use pod affinity to ensure that a group of pods co - schedule. for example, in # 18450 one element of a possible solution is to say " x can only run on a machine with y, and y can only run on a machine with x " ( so that if you kill x or y, the other one reloads, once we implement that behavior ). but such a rule will allow neither of them to ever schedule, since neither will be allowed to " go first. " fixing this is not high priority. cc / @ kevin - wangzefeng

We need to refactor the scheduler.. this is originally by daniel smith ( @ lavalamp ) : - store pods under / registry / pods / < podid >, or some other path _ not _ having a machine name in the path. - pod _ registry, instead of synchronously scheduling a pod, asks the scheduler only if the pod is feasible before accepting it. - scheduler is responsible for populating [ inline _ code ] according to the machine that the pod should be running on. this is done using compareandswap to ensure scheduler data integrity. - a control loop is responsible for syncing the currentstate. hostname field given the contents of the [ inline _ code ] directories - we expand the podstatus field ; this is just a suggestion of the sort of things that we should have : - admitted : the pod has been admitted to the system. - assigned : the scheduler has assigned it to a machine, we're waiting for the machine to start it. - running : it is running on the assigned machine. - stopped : something went wrong ( we lost a machine? ) and this pod will be rescheduled - completed : a state for the future, when we want to indicate that a pod was run once, as requested. - infeasible : the pod can no longer be fit anywhere.

title: Post-Quantum Cryptography Readiness Observations & Recommendations (Research)
body:
### What would you like to be added?

This issue shares research-based observations on post-quantum cryptography (PQC) readiness
in Kubernetes, based solely on publicly available code and documentation.

This is NOT a vulnerability report and does not include exploitation, attack paths, or
sensitive configuration details. The intent is awareness, future-readiness, and community
discussion aligned with NIST PQC transition guidance.

Observations:
• Cryptographic usage is distributed across multiple layers
• There is no centralized crypto inventory or ownership map
• No defined crypto agility or PQC migration framework
• No governance-level visibility into algorithm lifecycle

Recommendations:
• Consider adding a crypto inventory layer
• Define crypto ownership and lifecycle policy
• Track NIST PQC migration readiness
• Introduce crypto agility abstractions
• Document PQC roadmap for operators

Why this matters:
Quantum-safe transitions are multi-year efforts. Early visibility reduces long-term risk.

Happy to refine or contribute to documentation if helpful.

### Why is this needed?

Post-quantum cryptography (PQC) transitions are multi-year efforts that require early visibility and planning. 
Today, Kubernetes uses strong cryptography, but cryptographic usage is distributed across many layers 
(control plane, components, SDKs, dependencies), making long-term migration and governance difficult to track.

This enhancement is needed to:
- Improve visibility into cryptographic usage and ownership
- Enable crypto agility and algorithm lifecycle management
- Align Kubernetes with NIST post-quantum transition guidance
- Reduce future migration risk by identifying readiness gaps early
- Support operators and maintainers with clear, documented PQC readiness signals

This is not related to an exploitable vulnerability. 
It is a forward-looking readiness and governance improvement to help Kubernetes remain secure over the next decade.

Consider adding tracing support for OpenTracing (or similar). in 1. 3 we took most of the fat out of the internal apiserver and client machinery. however, we have fairly complex internal flows for controllers, caches, the watches, and other distribution mechanisms that are more difficult to trace / profile. in addition, we are adding larger numbers of control loops and feedback mechanisms into the state of the system - we are seeing more inconsistent outcomes that are hard to reason about. for 1. 4, i think it would be valuable to broaden the traces started in # 8806, possibly by adding opentracing support. it would also give us a bit more contextual information in failures. we would also need to consider how traces could propagate across control loops, such as whether we do level driven traces from the kubelet or elsewhere.

Provide a "roadmap" for what users can do post install (+ example).. " next steps " roadmap ( post - installation - & - examples info ) : need to provide a high - level, general path that applies to all users for moving forward with k8s ( ie. install and example done, now what? ). examples : - you created a cluster on a single node, see how to scale to meet your production needs : - point to creating more nodes, clusters - sharing cluster access - security, etc. - now you can set up : - configuration management tools? - networking, security, performance related configuration? - migrate to production? - > mention and point to the " planning and design considerations "

Consider a kind of Service that ignores readiness. this is mostly motivated by petset. currently we create a governing service that is responsible for the network identity of each pet. the requirements of this governing service differ from a normal service in the following ways : 1. pets have internal protocols to notice peer health, and a list of different checks ( eg : http : / / www. cloudera. com / documentation / enterprise / 5 - 4 - x / topics / cm _ ht _ zookeeper _ server. html ). in kube, peers use dns to communicate. so we don't want a readiness check failure to remove the pet from dns and abruptly cut it off from the set. 2. the " governing service " is headless so kube - proxy doesn't need to nat the service ip. 3. clients will not be using this service, so it doesn't matter that unready pets show up in dns under the svcname sub domain. in addition to these, there's one important reason some pets need to have dns before readiness. to provide the guarantees required to safely bootstrap a pet, we need : 1. pet0 starts before pet1.. 2. don't start pet1 till pet0 is running / ready 3. when pet1 starts, it sees pet0 in dns the easiest way to guarantee 3 today is to do one of : - poll in the entrypoint of pet0, till it sees itself - poll in the init container of pet0, till it sees itself - poll in the init containers of pet { 1.. n - 1 } till it sees all previous pets third option is not a great idea because we don't know who else is supposed to exist, and for the first 2 to work with a readiness probe, we need a dns record before the service is ready.

Initial kube-up support for VMware's Photon Controller. this is for : https : / / github. com / kubernetes / kubernetes / issues / 24121 photon controller is an open - source cloud management platform. more information is available at : http : / / vmware. github. io / photon - controller / this commit provides initial support for photon controller. the following features are tested and working : - kube - up and kube - down - basic pod and service management - networking within the kubernetes cluster - ui and dns addons it has been tested with a kubernetes cluster of up to 10 nodes. further work on scaling is planned for the near future. internally we have implemented continuous integration testing and will run it multiple times per day against the kubernetes master branch once this is integrated so we can quickly react to problems. a few things have not yet been implemented, but are planned : - support for kube - push - support for test - build - release, test - setup, test - teardown assuming this is accepted for inclusion, we will write documentation for the kubernetes. io site. we have included a script to help users configure photon controller for use with kubernetes. while not required, it will help some users get started more quickly. it will be documented. we are aware of the kube - deploy efforts and will track them and support them as appropriate.

title: [sig-windows] kube-proxy: Empty sourceVip causes broken NatPool occasionally, breaking LoadBalancer hairpinning
body:
### What happened?

Occasionally on newer Windows Server 2019 OS builds, Windows Pods experience connection timeouts when attempting to access a Kubernetes LoadBalancer VIP that routes back to a pod on the exact same node (hairpinning).
When this issue happened, the [INLINE_CODE] for the LoadBalancer policy is incorrectly set to the VIP itself instead of the Node's IP address. Because the backend pod sees the VIP as the source IP, it sends its reply back to the VIP. The Windows virtual switch (HNS) intercepts this reply, treats it as a brand-new inbound LoadBalancer request, and routes it into an infinite loop (or drops it), causing the connection to time out.

### What did you expect to happen?

Pod-to-LB hairpin traffic should always route correctly via a NatPool built with the Node IP.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

It occurs occasionally, so hard to reproduce consistently. 
1. Deploy a LoadBalancer service with local endpoints.
2. Run hnsdiag list loadbalancers on the host. Observe the NatPool uses the External VIP instead of the Node IP because "SourceVip" is "".

### Anything else we need to know?

1. Empty [INLINE_CODE] breaks hairpin routing on newer Windows HNS kernels.
In [INLINE_CODE], [INLINE_CODE] is an empty string "".
[CODE_BLOCK]
When [INLINE_CODE] passes "" to the Windows Host Compute Network (HCN) API:
* Sometimes (older versions) Windows HNS defaulted an empty SourceVIP to the Node IP. Hairpinning worked.
* Occationally Windows HNS default an empty SourceVIP to the Frontend VIP. Hairpinning breaks due to the routing loop.

title: Improve API serialization testdata fixtures for parameter-only encoded types
body:
Some types like GetOptions, ListOptions, PatchOptions are only encoded to parameter query strings

Because these types are registered into runtime.Scheme, they are currently tested as serialized to json, yaml, and proto (but *not* query parameters) in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/tree/master/staging/src/k8s.io/api/testdata

That produced spurious proto diffs in PRs like https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/136657 for ListOptions

1. Identify the types we don't serialize to proto (GetOptions, ListOptions, PatchOptions, I think) and do serialize to query parameters
2. Exclude those from proto round-tripping and serialization
3. Add tests to cover the stability of their query parameter serializations

/cc @deads2k

title: Autoscaling a custom resource which does not create pods
body:
If someone has a custom resource which does not create pods but does have a scale subresource, it would be nice to be able to scale it based only on a custom metric. Currently this is not possible with HorizontalPodAutoscaler since it needs to list pods and does not just trust what the scale subresource tells it.

This would mean ignoring the implementation details of whatever the custom resource controller creates under the hood and just use the status of the scale subresource.

title: etcd watcher scalability or improve decode efficiency
body:
### What would you like to be added?

**Context**
We are developing a Custom Resource Definition (CRD) controller that utilizes the standard list-watch (informer) mechanism. Under high workload conditions, we are observing significant latency in the initial notification trigger for reconciliation loops.

**Observations**
Upon inspecting the Kubernetes API server logs, we identified a high volume of the following warning messages:

`"Fast watcher, slow processing. Probably caused by slow decoding, user not receiving fast, or other processing logic"
`

This suggests a bottleneck where the API server is generating events faster than they can be decoded or consumed. While the log message mentions "slow decoding," our monitoring indicates that the controller itself is not CPU-bound or busy; rather, it appears starved of events because the API server cannot push them efficiently.

**Current Investigation**
We noticed that starting in Kubernetes v1.31, the feature gate ConcurrentWatchObjectDecode was introduced to address decoding bottlenecks by parallelizing the decoding of watch events. However, the current implementation hardcodes the concurrency limit to 10 workers. And the incoming/outgoing bufSize are also hardcoded to 100.

We are seeking the guidance if we could increase the hardcoded settings to improve the watcher efficiency, and whether k8s could provide a feature or guidance how to tune this case, e.g. improve the decoding efficiency.

### Why is this needed?

The controller is being starved of timely updates because the API server cannot produce events efficiently.

similar_issues.text: Create a cache in apiserver to improve its performance. # # background while running kubernetes on 100 - node cluster, the main bottleneck is the apiserver. for example, starting a replication controller with 3000 pods ( 100 nodes, 30 pods per node ) on the empty cluster lasts almost 20 minutes, and the cpu of 4 - core master is 100 % saturated for all that time. looking at the profiles, more than 50 % of cpu is spent on decoding objects coming from etcd ( i. e. decoding jsons ). i don't think we can do much with decoding itself, but what we can do is to limit the number of decodings we perform. for example, imagine a 100 - node cluster and say one pod has just changed. what happens currently ( which i think is reasonable ) is that all kubelets are listening to pods that are assigned to them. this however translates to opening watch for all pods, and filtering them at the apiserver based on the label / field selectors. this means that the particular change of a pod will be read from etcd 100 times, each time we independently decode it, apply labels and send it ( to at most one kubelet ). note that we're decoding the same pod read from etcd 100 times, which is a clear waste of resources. # proposal my proposal is to create some kind of cache in the apiserver. the approach i am suggesting is : 1. the cache is used only for reading ( writing doesn't read or modify cache ) 2. the cache is storing decoded api objects ( whether we will be storing all objects or just objects of some particular types is tbd ) together with their etcd index ( modifiedindex ) 3. the cache is storing at most one version of the object with a given key ( the newest one ). 4. when we read an object from etcd ( either via get or watch ) we : - send a request to etcd - if the returned version ( response contains modifiedindex value as an explicit field ) is the same as currently stored in cache, we don't need to decode it and simply return the value from the cache - if the returned version is newer ( modifiedindex is monotonically increasing ) we decode it an update the cache with the new version ( the old version ) - if the returned version is older, we simply have a cache miss and decode it without using

Watch flushing in chunked encoder may be inefficient at scale. we currently invoke flush on the http response after every watch event, in order to guarantee clients see watches immediately. that flush impacts throughput at scale, and may result in undesirable context switches in the server process. we should investigate deferred flushes, allowing the client to set an upper latency bound, or automatically adjusting the flush rate due to throughput. in a 8 core benchmark of watch decode performance, it's roughly 25 % faster not to flush than to flush ( 30us per iteration vs 40us per iteration ) - and time spent over 1m in that loop goes from 67 % waiting on syscall to 17 % waiting on sys call, with much more time spent in gc. @ wojtek - t @ kubernetes / sig - scalability

potential issue of API server cache. copy from discussion in https : / / github. com / kubernetes / kubernetes / pull / 23795 # issuecomment - 208176276 > when api server watched a event, it need to insert the event into all watchers'" input " channel, then each watcher has a goroute running in background to pop events from the " input " channel and sent it to the corresponding client. > > since we process event sequentially ( see [ processevent ] ( https : / / github. com / kubernetes / kubernetes / blob / master / pkg / storage / cacher. go # l362 - l363 ) ), if one watcher was blocked due to some reasons, all other watchers will be blocked! we can ensure correctness by terminating this blocked watcher if it timeout ( 5 seconds ) though, it may make watch really slow. for example, if we have 100 watcher watching a key, 10 watchers blocked and timeout by some reasons, the remaining watchers will receive the event after 50 seconds! may be artificial and speculative though, @ wojtek - t will send a pr to address this

Implement watch at apiserver level. implementing should give us significant performance improvements, because : - we avoid sending multiple watch requests to etcd that send as huge amount of unnecessary data ( e. g. currently all kubelets are watching for pods, but since filtering is done at the apiserver level, there are o ( # nodes ) watches to etcd open all the time, each of them sending all pods ) - on top of that we can build some indexer - see https : / / github. com / googlecloudplatform / kubernetes / issues / 4817 # issuecomment - 89437368 for more details cc @ lavalamp @ davidopp @ bprashanth @ timothysc

Write a reflector benchmark. throw load at etcd, limit it to a few cores, and open up some reflectors ( pod + node hostname would mimic kubelet, pod with / without hostname would be scheduler ). measure latency of time a change hits etcd to when it shows up in the reflector. it should be capable of catching https : / / github. com / googlecloudplatform / kubernetes / issues / 6059 as well as cases where the field / label matching logic has suddenly regressed. would be cool if it compared the overhead of a reflector with the raw etcd watch latency too, 2 benchmarks would achieve that, one with the raw etcd helper and another with the reflector. @ lavalamp thoughts?

Kubernetes api, controller, and client performance work. this is a roundup issue for kubernetes 1. 4 and a tracker to orient folks on the ongoing work. it is focused on all components that touch the api, but not necessarily the total system. it also serves to identify areas where folks can get involved. track issues using [ labels performance and csi - api - machinery ] ( https : / / github. com / kubernetes / kubernetes / issues? utf8 = & q = label % 3aarea % 2fperformance + label % 3a % 22team % 2fcsi - api + machinery + sig % 22 + ) # # # ongoing efforts major focus : we want to get to our target cluster size metrics ( 5k nodes and 300k pods ) in 1. 4 or 1. 5, and we are within an order of magnitude of that with 1. 3 in many dimensions. areas of attack : we are mostly cpu bound on the controllers and api servers today, and most of that is overhead due to garbage collection. we also have had a fair number of contention areas that were algorithmic or lock related in the core components. we've got a good feedback loop for identifying critical bottlenecks, but we could probably stand to get more profiles and metrics gathered from the high scale systems. - reduce the cpu and garbage created by clients and the api server when handling api requests - introduce protobuf - [ complete # 8132 ] used for most api objects when talking between client and server - [ inprogress for 1. 5 ] use protobuf for storage format - handle mixed content type storage ( objects that embed other objects like templates or third party resources ) - [ inprogress # 27258 ] handle optional slices and maps correctly in protobuf - [ inprogress ] ( https : / / github. com / gogo / protobuf / issues / 174 ) investigate use of string arena unmarshalling in protobuf to avoid [ ] byte - > string allocations in decode - optimize the conversion, defaulting, and decoding code paths - [ complete ] ( https : / / github. com / kubernetes / kubernetes / issues / 25019 ) implement more efficient quantity, using int64 and better serialization - [ complete # 24966 ] remove the use of reflection in conversion

Create a cache in apiserver to improve its performance. # # background while running kubernetes on 100 - node cluster, the main bottleneck is the apiserver. for example, starting a replication controller with 3000 pods ( 100 nodes, 30 pods per node ) on the empty cluster lasts almost 20 minutes, and the cpu of 4 - core master is 100 % saturated for all that time. looking at the profiles, more than 50 % of cpu is spent on decoding objects coming from etcd ( i. e. decoding jsons ). i don't think we can do much with decoding itself, but what we can do is to limit the number of decodings we perform. for example, imagine a 100 - node cluster and say one pod has just changed. what happens currently ( which i think is reasonable ) is that all kubelets are listening to pods that are assigned to them. this however translates to opening watch for all pods, and filtering them at the apiserver based on the label / field selectors. this means that the particular change of a pod will be read from etcd 100 times, each time we independently decode it, apply labels and send it ( to at most one kubelet ). note that we're decoding the same pod read from etcd 100 times, which is a clear waste of resources. # proposal my proposal is to create some kind of cache in the apiserver. the approach i am suggesting is : 1. the cache is used only for reading ( writing doesn't read or modify cache ) 2. the cache is storing decoded api objects ( whether we will be storing all objects or just objects of some particular types is tbd ) together with their etcd index ( modifiedindex ) 3. the cache is storing at most one version of the object with a given key ( the newest one ). 4. when we read an object from etcd ( either via get or watch ) we : - send a request to etcd - if the returned version ( response contains modifiedindex value as an explicit field ) is the same as currently stored in cache, we don't need to decode it and simply return the value from the cache - if the returned version is newer ( modifiedindex is monotonically increasing ) we decode it an update the cache with the new version ( the old version ) - if the returned version is older, we simply have a cache miss and decode it without using
Add a simple master benchmark and a wrapper to run it.. it's better than nothing, @ lavalamp @ davidopp thoughts? i do plan to shove etcd in a cgroup and use more kubectl libraries in test _ utils.

title: Job admission plugin checks gang-scheduling parallelism guard when only one of GenericWorkload/WorkloadWithJob is enabled

## What happened?

The [INLINE_CODE] admission check in [INLINE_CODE] uses an AND condition to skip validation:

[CODE_BLOCK]

This means the gang-scheduling parallelism guard is active when **either** feature gate is enabled. Disabling only [INLINE_CODE] (or only [INLINE_CODE]) is not sufficient to bypass the check — both must be disabled.

If a user disables [INLINE_CODE] expecting to opt out of gang-scheduling admission behavior, the check still fires because [INLINE_CODE] is enabled (or vice versa).

## What did you expect to happen?

Disabling the relevant feature gate for the code path being exercised should be sufficient to skip the validation. For example, the [INLINE_CODE]-based path (line 133) only makes sense with [INLINE_CODE], and the owner-reference scan path (line 148) only makes sense with [INLINE_CODE]. Each branch should be gated independently on its corresponding feature gate, rather than both branches being gated on the OR of the two gates.

1. Disable [INLINE_CODE] feature gate, leave [INLINE_CODE] enabled.

### What happened?

We switched to using ES384 and ran into an issue with conformance testing where the ServiceAccountIssuerDiscovery testcase failed.

[CODE_BLOCK]

The testcase should not be more restrictive than the actual cluster code.

Enable ES384 and run the test.

Proposal: return resourceVersion in all API responses. extracted from https : / / github. com / googlecloudplatform / kubernetes / pull / 846 # issuecomment - 54387892. it would be useful to return a global resourceversion in all operation responses : get, post, put, delete. in the presence of multiple, potentially inconsistent apiservers and / or proxies for apiservers, it would provide a way for a client to assess whether an apiserver / proxy were behind. for example, a client may create an object ( post ) and then want to be able to observe its state ( get and / or watch ). however, if requests after the post were sent to another apiserver, that apiserver might not know about the object yet, in which case the read would fail. the client can't just blindly poll until it sees the object due to cases where the object were rapidly deleted for some reason. the suggestion from @ smarterclayton and @ lavalamp was to put this in the http header. however, i don't know of an [ existing header field ] ( http : / / www. w3. org / protocols / rfc2616 / rfc2616 - sec14. html ) that has the semantics we'd like. for example, last - modified and if - modified - since are time - based. if - match and etags are exact - match - based preconditions - - perhaps useful for put. ( as a side note, looking at this made me wonder whether our behavior is currently correct with respect to caching. ) expect is hop - by - hop. otoh, it's my understanding that custom headers are discouraged in restful apis. i'd be ok with just returning the resourceversion in json in the response body, which i believe is even allowed for [ delete ] ( http : / / stackoverflow. com / questions / 299628 / is - an - entity - body - allowed - for - an - http - delete - request ).

ServiceErrorHandler should emit apiversion aware status. with https : / / github. com / googlecloudplatform / kubernetes / pull / 6881, we are now returning json with status object, for paths that are not handled by the server. but the status object is encoded in the latest version. it should be encoded in the version that was requested by the user ( which can be computed from the path ). we need to update go - restful for that, so that restful. serviceerrorhandler is passed the request as well.

Document why all REST calls return resourceVersion. what is the meaning ( and the purpose ) of podlist resourceversion? - isn't it just the collection of current pods? in which circumstances does it change? when a new pod is added? when any pod is updated? is there any use case when the rest api user should refer to the collection's resourceversion and / or pass this version to the server? ( when do users pass a list of pods to the server? ) thank you.

title: [Bug]: Informer cache lag on PVC claim state in pv_controller can trigger premature volume deletion
body:
### What happened?
In [INLINE_CODE] ([INLINE_CODE] in [INLINE_CODE]), the controller inspects the local informer claim cache ([INLINE_CODE]) to verify if a claim bound to a PV is released before marking the volume released or performing volume cleanup.

**Race Window:**
If a claim state changes or is updated in the API server, but the local informer cache experiences watch delay, [INLINE_CODE] reads stale claim state from its cache and can proceed to release or delete a persistent volume prematurely.

### What did you expect to happen?
Before executing irreversible volume deletion or release actions, [INLINE_CODE] should re-verify the live PVC object against the API server.

title: Expose per-resource storage write revision metric for watch cache and informer lag
body:
[WatchCacheLag](https://perf-dash.k8s.io/#/?jobname=gce-5000Nodes&metriccategoryname=GenericMeasurements&metricname=WatchCacheLag) and InformerCacheLag compare [INLINE_CODE] against the global [INLINE_CODE].

When a resource has no writes while other resources mutate, its watch cache RV stays at the last write until an etcd bookmark arrives. Because etcd bookmarks are infrequent, P99 lag is inflated idle phases (see graph below for services. The flat 0s at beginning and end are the only time services are changed, and sawtooth happens during times without writes.)

![Watch cache delay sawtooth during idle resource phases](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jefftree/kubernetes/issue-assets/watch_cache_lag_services.png)

We should record the last written storage revision per resource (e.g. [INLINE_CODE]) on successful writes in [etcd3/store.go](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/etcd3/store.go) and compare [INLINE_CODE] against that metric instead of the global etcd revision.

/sig scalability
/sig api-machinery

similar_issues.text: Keep a rolling average on resource creation and initial notification via watch. * * scenario : * * controller x has a watch against kube - api - server on resource y client a creates a new y 1. kube - api - server creates a resource y in etcd 2. etcd acknowledges create and responds with y, y createdindex / modifiedindex mapped to resourceversion 3. kube - api - server is notified via a watch event from etcd that y exists 4. controller x is then notified that y exists * * goal : * * measure the time between when the kube - api - server knows the resource was created ( step 2 ) and when it is retold that the resource was created via a watch notification from etcd ( step 3 ). i think we could track this by recording the local kube - api - server time with the resource creationtimestamp for watch where the nodeaction is create. there have been a few issues where as the number of keys in etcd grows to n, the time it takes to get notified in the api - server for n + 1 resource appears to grow even when inside an etcd watch window, having a metric would make it easier to debug, but have encountered some issues where latency appears to ~ 20s in some cases where if reported could provide a dump of some metrics endpoint, it would have been easier to isolate the issue. * * caveats : * * i am most interested in measuring the time when inside of an etcd watch window ; so i think it's fine if we ignored the metric on list + watch scenarios. @ wojtek - t - have you done any measurements in this area?

Reduce number of list requests in watch-based cache. previously watch - based cache was re - listing all objects if it lost connection with apiserver. there is no good reason to do it, as it's possible that resourceversion is still within etcd watch window. this reduces load on apiserver by not hammering it with many list requests upon start. during manual tests in 100 - node cluster i've observed much lower latencies and less spiky cpu usage. refs # 6770 @ wojtek - t @ lavalamp @ bprashanth

scheduler cache: Node level aggregated pods' resource summary. this pr provides nodeinfocache which aggregates pods'resource request and provides node - level resource summary. it's intended to supplant system modeler for efficient lookup in [ inline _ code ]. as we indicated in # 18831 that it is the most time - consuming code path and optimizing it would result in 10x improvement. the interface defined in the cache is similar to system modeler and its pod lister. additionally, we also need update ( ) and getnodeinfo ( ). we have drawn the state machine explicitly to show the workflow and how it interacts with pod events. it would be pretty straight - forward to use this cache into related hooks when state changes happen. that say, when pod is assumed, added, updated, removed. then we can use the cache to optimize scheduler predicates [ inline _ code ].

Create a cache in apiserver to improve its performance. # # background while running kubernetes on 100 - node cluster, the main bottleneck is the apiserver. for example, starting a replication controller with 3000 pods ( 100 nodes, 30 pods per node ) on the empty cluster lasts almost 20 minutes, and the cpu of 4 - core master is 100 % saturated for all that time. looking at the profiles, more than 50 % of cpu is spent on decoding objects coming from etcd ( i. e. decoding jsons ). i don't think we can do much with decoding itself, but what we can do is to limit the number of decodings we perform. for example, imagine a 100 - node cluster and say one pod has just changed. what happens currently ( which i think is reasonable ) is that all kubelets are listening to pods that are assigned to them. this however translates to opening watch for all pods, and filtering them at the apiserver based on the label / field selectors. this means that the particular change of a pod will be read from etcd 100 times, each time we independently decode it, apply labels and send it ( to at most one kubelet ). note that we're decoding the same pod read from etcd 100 times, which is a clear waste of resources. # proposal my proposal is to create some kind of cache in the apiserver. the approach i am suggesting is : 1. the cache is used only for reading ( writing doesn't read or modify cache ) 2. the cache is storing decoded api objects ( whether we will be storing all objects or just objects of some particular types is tbd ) together with their etcd index ( modifiedindex ) 3. the cache is storing at most one version of the object with a given key ( the newest one ). 4. when we read an object from etcd ( either via get or watch ) we : - send a request to etcd - if the returned version ( response contains modifiedindex value as an explicit field ) is the same as currently stored in cache, we don't need to decode it and simply return the value from the cache - if the returned version is newer ( modifiedindex is monotonically increasing ) we decode it an update the cache with the new version ( the old version ) - if the returned version is older, we simply have a cache miss and decode it without using

shared controller informers. related to https : / / github. com / kubernetes / kubernetes / issues / 14978 this demonstrates how controllers which use an [ inline _ code ], would be able to share the same watch and store. a similar " setup and run " approach could be done for an [ inline _ code ] to share that cache. i found adding listeners here to be easier than intercepting at the watch interface ( problems with resourceversion ) or the reflector ( same plumbing, but you have to fan out to multiple stores ). we could also use the cache we build here to back several of the admission plugins that currently run their own lookup caches today. if there's interest, i can finish out the [ inline _ code ] and switch the low hanging fruit over. @ kubernetes / rh - cluster - infra @ smarterclayton @ liggitt @ wojtek - t

title: Search result navigation does not provide target selection/range to custom editors (webview editors)
body:
Problem:
When a file type is handled by a custom editor (contributes.customEditors / CustomTextEditorProvider or CustomEditorProvider), global Search results appear for matches inside the file. Clicking a match opens the file in the custom editor, but VS Code does not navigate to the specific match location (line/column/range).

Expected:
Clicking a Search match should navigate to that exact match location even when the file is opened with a custom editor. At minimum, VS Code should provide the target selection/range to the custom editor so the extension can reveal/highlight it.

Actual:
The custom editor opens, but receives no information about which Search result was clicked, so it cannot scroll/reveal.

Why this matters:
Without this ability VS Code might as well stop supporting custom editors anyway as they are never going to have parity with built-in ones. Users **strongly expect** Search results clicks to reveal the match location; lack of this breaks a core VS Code workflow for any custom editor file type and customers have already told us verbatim that's a show stopper and reason for churn no matter what other problems the custom editor might be solving.

Proposed solution:
Extend the custom editor open context to include target selection/range when opening is triggered with a location. 

E.g. add [INLINE_CODE] to the context passed to custom editor providers (or equivalent).

Happy to help validate the changes, just let me know.

P.S. My custom editor uses a JSON file format and the custom file extension '.kqlx'. These type of details shouldn't really matter, but just in case it's helpful.

Fix #294007 terminal gap. # # problem on macos with high - resolution displays, the integrated terminal could render a visible gap between the selection highlight and adjacent ui elements ( such as the terminal tabs list or panel divider ). this gap was inconsistent and sensitive to zoom level and devicepixelratio, sometimes appearing or disappearing as the zoom changed. # # root cause the issue was caused by a mismatch between how xterm. js renders the terminal content and how vs code computes the layout of the terminal container. specifically : - xterm rendering operates on cell - based dimensions that can result in fractional pixel widths when scaled ( zoom / dpr ) - container and adjacent ui elements use dom layout calculations with different rounding behaviour - this led to inconsistent alignment at the right edge of the terminal, causing a visible gap at certain zoom levels # # fix introduce an offset - column rendering approach : - xterm renders one additional column to ensure the right edge fully covers the available space - pty / process dimensions continue to use the base number of columns to preserve correct terminal semantics ( e. g. wrapping behaviour ) additional adjustments : - align width calculations between renderer and container - subtract one cell width when reporting pixel dimensions to the pty - refine viewport synchronization to run again on the next frame after resize / zoom events to stabilize layout # # testing added tests to ensure : - render column count and pty column count remain correctly separated - process creation uses base dimensions ( no offset leakage ) - computed selection gap remains within acceptable bounds # # result the selection highlight now consistently aligns with adjacent ui elements across zoom levels and devicepixelratio configurations, eliminating the visual gap.

title: Copilot Chat: add loading spin when messages are sending
body:
When I'm working in GitHub Codespaces, sending messages to Copilot have ~10s delay (probably due to network issues). In this period, I thought the message hadn't been sent because the UI did not respond. So I pressed Enter for 3 times. Then 10s later the generation started, cancelled and started.

This problem could be significantly improved if the send button could be set to loading and disabled when a request has been sent but no response has been received.

similar_issues.text: Text highlighted with double click intermittently can't be edited. hi before i continue i just want to say thanks for all the hard work on making visual studio code a fantastic editor. i prefer it to webstorm, atom, sublime and anything else! ok to the main point, i have noticed what i think is a bug. when editing simple js files ( although not tried with other languages ), if i double click a word ( to highlight it ) and then start tying ( i. e. to replace it ), it sometimes ignores my typing. i'm using the standard dark theme and i have noticed that when this is the case, the highlight is a slightly different colour to the normal editable selected text highlight. i have also noticed that is happens more often if i double click quickly on a word, as opposed to if i double click more slowly. i have a feeling that because this is running on electron and essentially some kind of web application, maybe there is a race condition of sorts where if i double click too fast, the electron framework detects a select " span element " as opposed to the editor detecting that i'm highlighting a word for editing. it might be a bug in the underlying electron framework and not vs code itself, but i have no idea, just suggesting. i have asked a friend who uses atom on the same setup as me ( also uses electron ) and he says he can't replicate, but he did say he uses a plugin which highlights the same words as the selected word ( https : / / atom. io / packages / highlight - selected ). for additional information that might be of relevance in reproducing the issue, i am using vs code 0. 10. 6 ( latest release ), mac os x ( version 10. 10. 5 ), using the application in full screen mode ( i. e. command + ctrl + f ) and using an external usb mouse.

title: Simple Browser: handle Electron `login` event for HTTP Basic/Digest Auth
body:
## Problem

When opening a URL protected by HTTP Basic Auth in the Simple Browser, the user gets a blank page or a 401 error. No credential prompt is shown.

This happens because the Electron [[INLINE_CODE] event](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/api/web-contents#event-login) on [INLINE_CODE] is not handled for webview panels. The underlying Chromium engine fully supports auth prompts — they're simply not wired up.

Previously reported in #139342 (auto-closed due to insufficient upvotes, no design decision was made).

## The fix

Electron already emits a [INLINE_CODE] event when a [INLINE_CODE] encounters an HTTP 401 with a [INLINE_CODE] header. A minimal working implementation:

[CODE_BLOCK]

I’ve tested this by patching the main process entry point on VSCodium 1.112.x. It works for Basic Auth, Digest Auth, handles concurrent requests (multiple resources behind auth on the same page), and only prompts once per host (credentials cached in memory for the session).

## Why this matters

- **Remote development workflows** frequently involve sites behind Basic Auth (staging environments, internal tools, CI dashboards). The Simple Browser is the only integrated option; falling back to an external browser defeats its purpose.
- **AI-assisted development**: AI coding agents (GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, Cursor, etc.) increasingly rely on the Simple Browser to interact with web applications during development. Without auth support, they cannot access protected environments, limiting agentic workflows.
- **Trivial to implement**: the plumbing is already there in Electron. It's a matter of listening to an event that's currently ignored.

## Suggested implementation

1. Listen for [INLINE_CODE] on webview [INLINE_CODE] in the Electron main process
2. Show a credential prompt using VS Code's native QuickInput API (username + password fields)
3. Cache credentials per host for the session
4. Optionally persist via [INLINE_CODE]

title: Add suppressConfirmation option to updateWorkspaceFolders()
body:
## Problem

[INLINE_CODE] always shows a confirmation dialog when replacing the root folder because [INLINE_CODE] calls [INLINE_CODE], which includes a user veto step. There is no way to suppress this programmatically.

Extensions that manage workspace folder transitions (worktree switching, session isolation, etc.) cannot do seamless folder swaps without the user clicking through a dialog every time.

## Context

PR #292783 by @bpasero already solved this for agent sessions — it calls [INLINE_CODE] directly to bypass the dialog in that context. This is the same pattern, generalized as an API option.

## Approach

Add an optional [INLINE_CODE] flag to [INLINE_CODE]. When set, [INLINE_CODE] calls [INLINE_CODE] instead of [INLINE_CODE]. Extension hosts still restart normally — only the dialog is skipped.

The change threads through: [INLINE_CODE] → [INLINE_CODE] → [INLINE_CODE] → [INLINE_CODE] → [INLINE_CODE] (electron-browser).

## Current workaround

The [git-shell-helpers](https://github.com/RockyWearsAHat/github-shell-helpers) extension patches [INLINE_CODE] at runtime to replace the [INLINE_CODE] call with [INLINE_CODE] in [INLINE_CODE]. This breaks on every VS Code update and requires re-patching.

## References

- PR #292783 — @bpasero's agent session implementation (same pattern)

title: [Bug] CWE-79 XSS in Notebook Renderer: kernel output HTML reaches element.innerHTML via passthrough TrustedTypes (webviewPreloads.ts:2989) — known-accepted
body:
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

- VS Code Version: 1.121.0
- OS Version: All platforms

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Clone Visual Studio Code at commit [INLINE_CODE].
2. Navigate to [INLINE_CODE], line 2989.
3. Open a notebook connected to a kernel that returns a [INLINE_CODE] output cell containing [INLINE_CODE].
4. Observe that the script tag passes through the TrustedTypes passthrough policy, is inserted via [INLINE_CODE], and executes in the notebook webview.

[reproduce.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27959179/reproduce.zip)

**Description:**
The Notebook renderer webview assigns kernel output HTML to [INLINE_CODE] at [INLINE_CODE] via a passthrough TrustedTypes policy (line 1118: [INLINE_CODE]). The full data flow is: kernel output → [INLINE_CODE] → [INLINE_CODE] (passthrough) → [INLINE_CODE], with no sanitization applied at any stage. Tagged known-accepted by the project team. Reporting for awareness.

**Affected file:** [INLINE_CODE]
**Line:** 2989
**Commit:** 39e6e450164538bcad6962c82179334e715c5dda

At line 2987, the rendering condition checks [INLINE_CODE] (RenderOutputType.Html). Line 2988 calls [INLINE_CODE] — where the [INLINE_CODE] TrustedTypes policy (defined at line 1118) returns the input value unchanged. Line 2989 assigns the result as a string to [INLINE_CODE]. Because no sanitization occurs at any point in this chain, a malicious Jupyter kernel or compromised renderer extension can inject [INLINE_CODE] tags or event-handler payloads that execute in the notebook webview. The project suppresses the CodeQL finding: [INLINE_CODE]

**Impact:**
Attacker-controlled HTML/JS injected into VS Code notebook output — potential for script execution in the notebook renderer webview, access to the [INLINE_CODE] API, workspace data exfiltration, or extension privilege escalation depending on sandbox configuration.

title: Agents view: session resume fails with "Error during execution" when no git repo
body:
## Bug Description

When resuming a CLI-created Claude Code session from the Agents view, the session fails with:

[CODE_BLOCK]

The underlying SDK error is:
[CODE_BLOCK]

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a Claude Code session via CLI in a directory without a git repository (e.g., [INLINE_CODE])
2. Open VS Code Insiders (no workspace open)
3. Open the Agents view — the CLI session appears in the session list
4. Click on the session and send a message (e.g., "hi")
5. **Result**: "Error: Error during execution" is displayed

## Root Cause

When the session has no associated git repository, [INLINE_CODE] creates a fallback workspace folder with URI [INLINE_CODE] ([line 1266](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/copilotChatSessions/browser/copilotChatSessionsProvider.ts#L1266)). [INLINE_CODE] then registers this as a real workspace folder.

In the Copilot extension, [INLINE_CODE] sees one workspace folder and uses its [INLINE_CODE] as the Claude SDK [INLINE_CODE]. On Windows, [INLINE_CODE] resolves to [INLINE_CODE]. The SDK uses this invalid [INLINE_CODE] to locate the session file on disk, looking in [INLINE_CODE] instead of the correct project directory.

## Environment

- VS Code Insiders 1.122.0
- Windows 11
- Claude Code CLI sessions created via Agent Maestro proxy

## Fix

Filter [INLINE_CODE] to only include [INLINE_CODE] scheme URIs in [INLINE_CODE], so virtual/unknown workspace folders are excluded. See PR.

title: [accessibility] screen reader cannot announce results while navigating between results in search box
body:
- VS Code Version: 1.123.0 (system setup)
- OS Version: windows 11 pRO

Steps to Reproduce:

1. NVDA is opened.
2. A project is opened with VSCode.
3. Search box is opened with CTRL + Shift + F and a text known to be in the project is entered into the search box.
4. To reach results, tab is pressed until the treeview showing results is reached.
5. When we focus on the treeview, NVDA tells us, for example: 48 results in 4 files - Search: foot
6. {regression} User navigates between results with arrow keys but NVDA cannot announce the search results, moreover even in object navigation (NVDA + num4/num6 etc.) these cannot be captured by NVDA.
 NOTE: navigation works correctly but NVDA seems unable to access the objects here.

findings:

This regression probably occurred in version 123.0. There was no such problem in the previous version.

title: Window close: old UI flashes for a split second
body:
## Feedback

> The old ui shows up for a split second when you close a window

**Source**: #workbench-refresh-feedback — Tyler Leonhardt on 2026-07-10
**Reactions**: 😮 ×1, 👍 ×1

---

## Context

When closing a window, the pre-refresh ("old") UI is briefly visible for a split second before the window disappears. This flash of unstyled/old content is jarring during the close transition.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Closing a window does not flash the old (pre-refresh) UI
- [ ] The window close transition remains visually consistent with Modern UI styling

similar_issues.text: Do not hide interaction prompt when window loses focus.. when install an extension, it takes quite a long time to load the list for me. but the only thing i can do is staring at the progress bar and waiting. once i switch to another window, the prompt disappears, and i will have to wait again.

Should we auto-reload from time to time?. here is a crazy thought : if we would be better at persisting view state ( e. g. find widget, commit message, undo / redo stack, etc. ). and if it would be a good time ( e. g. no unsaved files, no debug session, user is idle for > 10 min ).... maybe we could auto - reload the window after x hours? @ bpasero @ joaomoreno @ egamma @ jrieken thoughts?

Provide an option to keep quick open open on focus lost. when i try to switching between windows using [ inline _ code ] quickopen panel ( which i opened with [ inline _ code ] ) close, it's a little annoying

Improve workspace management. we need to improve the way that the users workspace is managed. the following ( non - exhaustive ) list of items describes what we should do : - [ x ] - when a user clicks an editor close button we should show the file that was previously opened in that editor ( we could also consider showing a set of file thumbnails and allow the user to choose the file to open ) - [ ] - we should explore better ways to indicate which editor is currently active - [ x ] - we should explore better ways to move and open files in different editors. for example, should the working files list also indicate which files are currently open and in which editor - [ ] - we should ensure that whenever the user opens a folder that the whole workspace opens up in the exact same state it was in when they last closed it ( including all files, viewports and active viewlet )

UI - "Close all but this" context menu option for working files. * * owner : * * @ bpasero * * issue : * * # 2643 * * assignees : * * - [ x ] windows @ gregvanl - [ x ] os x @ joaomoreno - [ x ] linux @ isidorn * * details : * * - there is a new action " close other files " in the context menu of a working file to do that - there is a new global action " close other files " that looks at the currently active opened editor and tries to close all files that are not that one - verify that you still get confirm boxes popping up in case one of the " other " files getting closed is dirty or untitled.

title: agent host: one representation and one cascade rule for customization enablement
body:
Follow-up cleanup from the scoped-enablement work (#330566, #330715).

## Problem

There are three representations of "is this on?" in session state:

- [INLINE_CODE] ([INLINE_CODE])
- [INLINE_CODE] ([INLINE_CODE])
- [INLINE_CODE] on [INLINE_CODE] and [INLINE_CODE] ([INLINE_CODE], [INLINE_CODE])

The tell that this is one representation too many is that the protocol doc comment has to *teach a rule you must memorize*:

> the **effective** enabled state of a plugin child is the plugin's derived enabled value and [INLINE_CODE], so a disabled plugin disables every child regardless of each child's own flag. A directory child instead uses the directory's [INLINE_CODE] value and its own flag.

Two different cascade rules depending on container type, neither enforced anywhere.

Predictably, consumers hand-roll the cascade. The same expression appears in at least three places across two files:

[CODE_BLOCK]

- [INLINE_CODE]
- [INLINE_CODE]
- [INLINE_CODE]

There are ~32 enablement-derivation sites in total across the agent host and its consumers. Any one of them getting the cascade subtly wrong is a silently-wrong enabled state in the UI or, worse, at the SDK boundary.

## Suggestions

**Minimum viable:** export a single [INLINE_CODE] in [INLINE_CODE] and use it everywhere the cascade is currently re-derived. Cheap, no protocol change, removes the duplication.

**Better, if a protocol change is acceptable:** collapse to one representation so directories and plugins cascade identically and the doc comment no longer needs to describe two rules. Note the protocol lives in [microsoft/agent-host-protocol](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-host-protocol) ([INLINE_CODE] is canonical; vscode's [INLINE_CODE] mirrors it), so this needs a change there first.

title: Agent Host chat input reverts while typing after draft sync rejection
body:
## Problem

Text typed into the chat input for an Agent Host session can repeatedly disappear, leaving the input reverted to an earlier prefix. In the reported case, the input kept returning to [INLINE_CODE] as additional words were typed.

The Agent Host protocol logs show this sequence:

1. [INLINE_CODE] was the last server-confirmed [INLINE_CODE] value.
2. The UI remained open and editable after the host considered the backing session explicitly deleted.
3. Each longer draft was sent optimistically through [INLINE_CODE].
4. The host rejected each action with [INLINE_CODE].
5. Subscription state returned to the last confirmed draft, and that state was reflected back into the live chat input.

As a result, every newly typed suffix disappeared shortly after draft synchronization ran. The same state transition can also occur when reconnect processing replaces optimistic state with a fresh server snapshot.

## Expected

Failure to synchronize a draft should not destroy text currently being edited locally.

## Actual

A protocol rollback or snapshot can be interpreted as an incoming draft update and overwrite the live editor contents. This can make the input appear impossible to type into while the underlying session remains stale or unavailable.

(Written by Copilot)

title: Codex Agent Host fails in workspaces using only an extension-registered filesystem
body:
### Description

Our extension registers a custom filesystem provider. When a VS Code workspace contains only resources from this extension-contributed filesystem, Codex Agent Host fails to start a turn with:

[INLINE_CODE]

The regular Codex extension handles the same workspace successfully.

**Steps to Reproduce**

- Create a new VS Code workspace.
- Add a file from an extension-registered filesystem provider.
- Ensure the workspace contains only resources from that filesystem.
- Enable: [INLINE_CODE]
- Start a Codex Agent Host session and send Hello.
- Start a session using the regular Codex extension and send the same message.

**Actual Result**

Codex Agent Host fails with:
[INLINE_CODE]

The regular Codex extension starts and processes the request successfully.

**Expected Result**

Codex Agent Host should support workspaces backed by extension-registered filesystem providers, or gracefully handle non-native workspace URIs without passing an invalid or missing absolute path to Codex.

title: Agent Host: permission mode can race managed-settings resolution
body:
## Type of issue

Bug

## Problem

A Copilot Agent Host session can attempt to apply the VS Code-configured [INLINE_CODE] permission mode before the SDK/runtime has finished resolving managed settings. The runtime then rejects the mode and the turn fails with:

[CODE_BLOCK]

This appears intermittently and is most visible when managed settings disable bypass permissions or resolution temporarily enters a fail-closed state.

## Current behavior

- [INLINE_CODE] derives [INLINE_CODE] from root/session configuration.
- [INLINE_CODE] sends that value through [INLINE_CODE] at turn start.
- Managed settings are resolved independently by the runtime. The [INLINE_CODE] event is currently projected into session sandbox policy, but not into effective approval/permission state.
- [INLINE_CODE] logs and continues when the managed-settings event has not arrived before post-launch sandbox configuration.

The resulting state can briefly advertise or select Allow All while the runtime has already disallowed bypass, causing the SDK RPC to reject rather than clamping the effective mode before the turn starts.

## Expected behavior

Session startup and turn preparation should have an authoritative managed-permission boundary. VS Code should not request [INLINE_CODE] until managed settings are resolved and permit bypass. A restrictive or fail-closed result should update the effective permission mode and picker state before sending the turn.

## Related

- #335928 tracks picker/runtime behavior for [INLINE_CODE].
- #330036 was a separate managed-settings schema failure involving [INLINE_CODE].
- #330349 handled legacy-setting transport ordering; it does not establish a runtime managed-settings readiness barrier for permission mode.

title: Bound Linux smoke-test disk diagnostics to avoid job timeout
body:
## Summary

The Linux Electron Tests job in build [475743](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/a6d41577-0fa3-498e-af22-257312ff0545/_build/results?buildId=475743&view=logs&j=193e9987-1fae-53fa-a82e-3ae14c27c30d&t=c6def06e-f043-549c-e923-f5085dee008a) hit its 50-minute timeout after the pre-smoke diagnostic spent 12m40s running [INLINE_CODE].

All unit, integration, and smoke tests completed successfully. The later Component Governance task was canceled only because the diagnostic consumed the remaining job budget.

## Evidence

First attempt on [INLINE_CODE]:

- [INLINE_CODE]: 23:01:42–23:14:22 (**12m40s**)
- [INLINE_CODE]: succeeded in 10m52s
- [INLINE_CODE]: started with ~19 seconds left and was canceled by the job timeout

Successful retry on [INLINE_CODE]:

- Same diagnostic: **43s**
- Component Governance: succeeded in 42s
- Overall Linux stage and build succeeded

The long interval is visible directly around:

[CODE_BLOCK]

## Source

The root traversal was added in #322903 / commit 24cb1a383384:

https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/build/azure-pipelines/linux/steps/product-build-linux-test.yml

[CODE_BLOCK]

The step has [INLINE_CODE], but no task or command timeout. A successful but slow [INLINE_CODE] therefore consumes the job timeout budget.

## Suggested fix

Preserve the disk-space diagnostics, but bound expensive traversals—for example with [INLINE_CODE] (and similarly bound the other [INLINE_CODE]/[INLINE_CODE] diagnostics), or add a short task-level timeout. Diagnostic collection should not be able to prevent test/post-test work from completing.

## Problem

I want MCP servers disabled globally and to opt individual workspaces into the servers they need.

Today, this means manually disabling every server, then re-enabling individual servers per workspace or session. There is not a clear place to see and manage those workspace choices.

- Provide an easy way to keep all MCP servers disabled by default as a user preference.
- Enable selected servers for a workspace without changing the global default.

This is a request for a configurable workflow, not a change to the default for everyone.

title: Managed enabledPlugins true does not force-enable an installed plugin
body:
## Problem

When the enterprise [INLINE_CODE] policy maps an installed [INLINE_CODE] identity to [INLINE_CODE], the plugin is still governed by the stored user or workspace enablement choice. A user can disable it, removing its contributed hooks, skills, tools, or other customizations even though organization policy requires it.

The inverse policy value already behaves differently: a plugin mapped to [INLINE_CODE] is disabled and cannot be re-enabled.

## Expected behavior

For plugins that are already installed and discovered:

- Managed [INLINE_CODE] force-enables the exact [INLINE_CODE] identity.
- Managed [INLINE_CODE] force-disables it.
- Local profile and workspace enablement writes cannot override either managed value.
- The underlying user choice is preserved and becomes effective again if the managed entry is removed.
- Plugins omitted from policy remain user-controlled; the setting stays additive rather than becoming an allowlist.
- A force-enabled plugin cannot be disabled or uninstalled through the plugin management UI.

## Verification

Configure three installed fixture plugins:

[CODE_BLOCK]

Leave a third plugin omitted from policy, and pre-seed [INLINE_CODE] as locally disabled.

Verify that:

1. [INLINE_CODE] is enabled and its switch is locked.
2. [INLINE_CODE] is disabled and its switch is locked.
3. The omitted plugin remains user-toggleable.
4. The required plugin has no uninstall action.
5. Removing the policy entries restores the stored local choices.
6. A same-named plugin from another marketplace does not inherit the managed decision.

Fixed by #337209.

## Scope

This issue covers enablement and management controls for plugins that are already installed and discovered. Installation or restoration of a missing required plugin is tracked separately in #337221. Failure behavior when a required plugin cannot be acquired is also outside this issue.
